transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry.

tell me your dream — however it comes back to you.
there was this old train going through snow at night, and i was sitting across from my grandfather. he’s been gone for years. he had this brown leather suitcase on his knees.
a brown leather suitcase on his knees. that's nice, the weight of it.
yeah. he had it open, and it was full of letters, hundreds of them, all addressed to me. he didn’t say anything, just held it out so i could see.
hundreds of them, and he didn't say a word.
right. and the train was so quiet. outside everything was white and blue. then it just stopped in the middle of a snowy field.
it just stopped. and then what? or was that the end?
we got off and walked through deep snow toward this red door standing on its own. no house, just the door in its frame. he gave me the suitcase and nodded at it.
a door standing on its own. that's the kind of thing that makes you pause.
i opened it and there was warm yellow light on the other side. and then i woke up.
warm light, after all that white and blue. that's lovely.
yeah, it was the first warm thing in the whole dream. i keep thinking about the look he gave me when he handed me the suitcase.
the look he gave you. how did it feel, when he handed it over?
like he was passing something on. not sad, not urgent. just sure.
not urgent, just sure. that sounds... steady.
it was. i didn’t feel scared at all, which is weird for a dream like that.
that makes me think about how you were in the dream. were you yourself?
yeah, i think i was just me. i don’t remember feeling younger or anything. he didn’t say a word the whole time, but it was like it was all right.
that's something in itself, that it was all right.
it really was. i guess that’s why the door and the warm light felt okay too, not weird.
if you could pause the dream on one moment, what would it be?
when he held the suitcase open toward me with all those letters. that’s the part i keep seeing.

so an old train at night, snow outside white and blue. your grandfather across from you, brown leather suitcase open on his knees, full of letters all addressed to you. he held it out without a word. the train stopped in a snowy field, you both walked through deep snow to a red door standing on its own. he gave you the suitcase and nodded. you opened the door and there was warm yellow light. it all felt steady, not scary, like he was passing something on.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
you got it right. only thing is the light was on the other side of the door, and it felt warm more than it looked bright. but yeah, that’s all of it.

warm more than bright. that's good to hold onto.

would you like to see it drawn?
yes, i would.

there are a few ways i could draw it.

a soft charcoal sketch, smudged charcoal over a blue-gray wash of snowy night. a weathered old photograph, faded sepia and blue like a photo left in the snow. a flat woodblock print, stark blocks of white, blue and black with a warm yellow symbol. or as it was in the dream, clear and true as a memory with the impossible plain as day. which feels closest, or would you describe your own?
as it was in the dream, clear and true as a memory. with the impossible plain as day.

i'll start with your grandfather, just him on his own.

i'm picturing an elderly man, soft and grandfatherly. that's my guess, nothing more. does that feel like him, or would you change anything?
soft and grandfatherly fits. i don’t remember exactly what he was wearing, so go with your guess.

i'm sketching your grandfather, the snowy field, the other side of the door, the brown leather suitcase, and the letters now — it'll appear on the right. only that, nothing else is being drawn yet.

for the carriage, i'm picturing an old train interior: rows of seats, a window showing the night outside. inside, just the seats, the window, and the open suitcase with the letters. the light is quiet and dim, night outside but the interior light i'm not sure of. these are my guesses. does any of that feel different, or would you leave it to me?
leave it to you. that all feels right, especially the quiet dim light inside. that matches how the train felt.

then the carriage stays as i've described it, with that quiet dim light. i'm glad it matched.

i'll draw it that way, and then i'll sketch the snowy field and the door on their own.
okay. i’d like that.
i'll get to work then. i'll let you know when it's ready.
sounds good.
take your time. i'll be right here.
thanks, berry.
of course.
these are really good. the snowy field with the door looks just how i remember it. the light through the door came out right too.

i'm so glad the field and the door came out right. the warm light was important.

your grandfather, the carriage, the suitcase with the letters?
the suitcase with the letters looks right. the carriage too. my grandfather is close, but he looks a little older than i remember.

good to hear the carriage and suitcase came out right.

i'll make your grandfather a touch younger, closer to how you remember him.
that's better. he looks more like i remember him now.
i'm redrawing your grandfather with that change — the new version will appear on the right. the rest are still on their way.
okay, no rush.
i'm on it. i'll let you know when the new one's ready.
thank you. i'll be here.
i'm working on it. i'll let you know as soon as it's ready.
alright, take your time.
i will.
oh, is it all redrawn now? just seeing the one so far.

no, just that one moment up so far — the old train going through snow at night. there are more moments still to come, but only that one is on the right now.

does it look the way you remember?
yeah, it does. the white and blue outside is exactly how it felt.
i'm glad it feels right. more moments will appear on the right soon.
i see that. looks like a few more are up now.

yeah, the suitcase full of letters, and the train stopping in the snow — they're both up now. there are 3 moments so far, 4 more still to come.

does that match how you saw them?
they do. especially the suitcase with all the letters, that's the part i keep thinking about.
that's the part that stays with you. i can see why.
what's the new one?

the new one is you and your grandfather walking through the deep snow toward the red door. that's 4 of 7 moments up now.

does it look the way you remember?
